options.metric: Annual number of persons killed, separately for motorists and cyclists
options.reason: Absolute counts make the year-by-year size of the mortality gap and changes in each group easy to compare.
options.answer: Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year from 2013 through 2025; in 2025, the counts were 81 motorists and 23 cyclists.

options.denominator: Cyclist deaths in the same year
options.reason: The ratio expresses the relative gap as a single value for each year, making changes in the gap easy to follow.
options.answer: Motorist deaths were 10.0 times cyclist deaths in 2013, the largest annual ratio, and 3.52 times cyclist deaths in 2025; the ratio stayed above 1 in every year.

options.metric: Each road-user type’s percentage share of the combined motorist and cyclist deaths
options.denominator: Motorist deaths plus cyclist deaths in the same year
options.reason: A within-year percentage view highlights how the mix of motorist and cyclist deaths shifts independently of the combined total.
options.answer: Cyclists accounted for the highest share of combined motorist and cyclist deaths in 2019, at 27.4%; their share in 2025 was 22.1%.

answer:
Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year from 2013 through 2025; in 2025, the counts were 81 and 23, respectively.
Motorist deaths were 10 times cyclist deaths in 2013—the largest annual ratio—and 3.52 times cyclist deaths in 2025.
Cyclists’ largest share of combined motorist and cyclist deaths was 27.4% in 2019; their share in 2025 was 22.1%.
